root_cause.text: The qla2xxx driver allows module unload to proceed while a fabric scan is in progress, and when the UNLOADING flag is set during that scan, the interrupt handler attempts to free DMA memory (dma_free_attrs) in interrupt context because the scheduled work item was not allocated, leading to a system crash.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states "The root cause of this was that there was a free (dma_free_attrs) in the interrupt context" due to the module unload setting the UNLOADING flag during fabric scan, preventing work item allocation and forcing a memory free in the interrupt handler. The patch adds a wait condition `(vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING)` to `qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready()` to delay module unload until the scan completes.

The patch adds a wait condition `(vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING)` to `qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready()` to delay module unload until the scan completes.

candidates.rationale: Part of the loop condition that waits for reset or dpc activity; when combined with the UNLOADING check, it prematurely exits during scan.
Continuation of the condition that normally would hold up unload; allowing break bypasses this guard.
Check for reset recovery state; combined with UNLOADING break, unload can proceed even if reset recovery is active.
Directly checks if a target scan is in progress; the break when UNLOADING is set allows unload while scan is active, leading to the crash.
This condition allows the loop to break early when unload is requested, overriding the scan-in-progress guard and permitting unload to proceed unsafely.
The break statement exits the wait loop, allowing module unload to continue while a fabric scan may still be running, which can cause DMA memory freeing in interrupt context.
The delay in the loop is not directly vulnerable but is part of the wait mechanism; its presence is irrelevant once the break occurs.

vuln_statements.explanation: Part of the loop condition that normally waits for reset or DPC activity; the early break when UNLOADING is set bypasses this guard, allowing unload while fabric scan may still be active.
Continuation of the loop condition checking mailbox busy; the break overrides this check, permitting module unload despite ongoing mailbox operations that may be part of the scan.
Checks for reset recovery state; the break when UNLOADING is set allows unload to proceed even if reset recovery is active, potentially leading to unsafe DMA operations in interrupt context.

Directly checks if a target scan is in progress; the premature break when UNLOADING is set allows module unload while a fabric scan is still running, which can cause DMA memory freeing in interrupt context and crash the system.

This condition causes an early exit from the wait loop when the UNLOADING flag is set, overriding the safety checks that would otherwise hold up unload until scan completes. This is the direct trigger for the vulnerability.

The break statement exits the wait loop, allowing module unload to continue while a fabric scan may still be in progress. This leads to freeing DMA memory in interrupt context, causing a system crash.
